According to the Sepsis-3 definition, sepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. The Sepsis-3 definition, published in 2016, emphasizes the importance of organ dysfunction in the diagnosis of sepsis. 

The Sepsis-3 definition includes three components: 

1. Suspected infection
2. Organ dysfunction
3. A combination of clinical criteria, such as the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score or the quick SOFA (qSOFA) score.

Source: "Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock: 2016." Intensive Care Med. 2016;42(12):361-379. doi: 10.1007/s00134-016-4688-7
